lines.dialogueText: On a quiet, rainy night.
Glyph sits at his desk seeking inspiration when a silent tear in reality opens near his bookshelf.
An ancient, pale light containing self-writing script forms a glowing rift before him.
Startled, Glyph drops his pen and instinctively reaches out into the yielding darkness.
Where — what is this place?
Aethelscript. The world beneath the language of all things. You would not have been pulled here if you were not meant to come.
I don't have long. Listen. We're the codewardens. We keep this world's Python Runes declared and true.
'Keep'? Past tense?
What does it do?
It doesn't break things. It un-writes them. It's already taken all four Sanctums. It's taken every codewarden but me.
So what am I supposed to do?
Take this. The Spellbook. Everything I know, in these pages. It teaches one lesson at a time.
And after I learn it?
Four Sanctums. Four Rune Crystals. Restore them, or Null Wraith finishes the job
I don't know where to start.
First is the Print Console where spoken truth becomes stone. Its Crystal governs manifestation, turning words into real, physical things” (Print Statements)
Next is the Vars Vault where things are given their name and value. Its Crystal controls identity, keeping the line drawn between something and nothing” (Variables and basic operations)
The Input Mists where the world actually listens and responds. Its Crystal governs communication, controlling the connection and the desire to answer” (Input handling)

Lastly, The Elif Labyrinth, where decisions are made and time actually progresses. Its Crystal controls order. Without it, nothing follows anythingthe world completely forgets how to take turns” (Conditionals and loops)
A guide is waiting in each Sanctum. Printessa. Variel. Evalyn. Whilow. Find them.
What about you?
I held on just long enough to find you. That's all I had left.
Wait-
Don't fear getting it wrong. Every error can be fixed. That's what separates you from Null Wraith. Rewrite what's broken.
A figure stands at the center of the console hall, her form flickering with printed characters that scroll faintly across her robes like a screen that never stops refreshing.
Another traveler came to read the walls with nothing left to say.
What happened to them? These tablets are blank.
Null Wraith erased them. Every statement that proved this place was real now gone.
How do I fix that?
Print it. If it isn't printed, it isn't true here.

In Python you write print("your message here"). The word print tells the console you are about to speak. The parentheses hold what you're saying. The quotation marks tell it your words are text, not a command.
Get the quotes wrong, open with one kind and close with another, and the console hears nothing at all. It has to match, start to finish.
Three missions remain on your tablet. Complete them and the gate answers.
I'll try.
Trying is how it starts.
Your tablet still holds what's left. Check it before you go further.
The Crystal at the center of the console hall catches the light of every restored statement and holds it. The floor stops flickering.
It just needed to know it was finished.
Don't we all. Remember that further in, the world only knows what you tell it.
You did well, traveler. Better than most who've stood where you're standing.
The Vars Vault is next. Follow the compass, it knows the way even if you don't.
The far gate opens. Printessa steps back into the scrolling light and does not follow.
Unassigned boulder, no mass, no destination. You're not one of mine.
No.
Good. I've catalogued enough of those today.
What is this place?
The Vars Vault. Nothing exists here without a name and a value. Null Wraith severed the bindings, now things drift.
How do I stop it?
Name it. Assign it a value. mass = 40 gives that boulder a mass. distance = 12 gives it a place to be measured from.
Names are case sensitive here. distance and Distance are two different things to the Vault, not the same thing spelled differently.
And a single equals sign only assigns. It doesn't ask whether two things are equal, that's a different question for a different day.
Noted.
Your tablet will keep count. Look before you leave.
Two bindings held, one Crystal left dark. Your tablet knows which.
Names and values settle back into place across the Vault. What was drifting is named again.
Named, valued, real. That's the Vault settled.
Well assigned, Glyph. Not everyone binds a thing correctly on the first try.
The Mists are next, and they're worse than they sound. The compass will keep you pointed the right way.
You won't get anything from this place by demanding it.
Then how?
Ask. Precisely. This place only answers what it's given.
input("Who approaches?") asks a question and waits. Whatever the Mists give back, it comes back as words, even if you asked for a number.
If you need a number instead of words, you have to say so yourself, int(input("...")), or the Mists will hand you digits that refuse to add.
That seems like a strange rule.
Every place has one. Ours is that it never assumes what you meant.
Three things left on your tablet. Ask this place exactly what it needs and it will answer.
The Mists won't fill your tablet in for you. Ask again.
The fog thins where it had settled thickest. The Mists' Crystal takes the last answer and holds it.
It answered. That's the Mists' Crystal settled.
You asked well. This place doesn't answer everyone that cleanly.
The Labyrinth won't forgive carelessness, and it's the last of them. The compass will take you there.
If you go left, one thing happens. Else, another. That's the whole maze.
And if I choose wrong?
You loop back and choose again. Null Wraith broke the conditions here, branches lead nowhere, loops don't close.
Indentation is the only wall in this maze. Line up wrong and the path doesn't exist, even if the words are right.
elif only gets asked if what came before it said no. Once one path answers, the rest stay quiet.
And a loop that never changes what it's checking never ends. Something inside it has to move, or you're just walking in place.
How do I fix that?
Read the condition first. Then decide.
Your tablet holds the last of it. One Crystal, still dark.
One line left. Read it before you move.
The Main Loop turns again, closing on itself the way it was always meant to. The last Crystal answers.
It remembers. That's the last Crystal answered.
What's after this?
Uncharted. But you have what you need.
And if I'm not ready?
Then you go anyway.
...undefined... undefined...
Not anymore.
...no space left to,
It's whole. The prophecy held.
...not gone... only unassigned...
...what was corrupted once... can be corrupted again...
Try it.
...you carry something now... I was never built to erase...
Understanding.
